_doc: Revert-verify mutants for vault-exodev ems__Bug 02355814, subject FilterExecutor.ts: arithmetic over a non-numeric operand is a type error (strict toNumericValue), and an operand node that is a numeric literal carried as text keeps its type (evaluateArithmeticOperand). Each mutant removes one guarantee and must redden exactly the axes in `expect`; M13–M20 are the wrong-but-plausible implementations named by the specification and its independent review. `tree`/`subject` are placeholders.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/infrastructure/sparql/executors/FilterExecutor.ts

M1_text_parsed_again._note: The defect itself, text half: a JS string operand is parsed by parseFloat again (numeric prefix taken). Every axis whose operand is a string constant, a function result or a substituted plain string goes red; A3 (typed date/time literals) and A8/A9 (numbers carried as text keep their type) do not. Specification: A16 (a BIND / subquery text constant is parsed again) and A20 ("2026-11-10" - "2026-11-01" as plain strings is 2026 - 2026 = 0, not an error) turn red too.

M2_any_literal_parsed._note: The defect itself, literal half: a Literal of ANY datatype is parsed by parseFloat (the old 'Try to parse as number anyway'). Dates become their year, a plain store literal "7" becomes 7. A15: COUNT(?t + 0) counts the coerced values again. Specification: A17 (VALUES literals of a non-numeric datatype are parsed) and A18 (the duration branches call toNumericValue on a store literal) turn red too.

M3_operand_type_dropped._note: Plausible wrong implementation 'strict toNumericValue only': the operand is evaluated as before, so a numeric literal the engine carries as text (xsd:double / float / derived-integer constant, a store number substituted by a bind join or EXISTS) reaches arithmetic as a bare string and is rejected — on either side of the operator (M8 / M9 drop one side each). Specification: A19 (every numeric constant of the 16 datatypes arrives as a bare string) turns red too.

M4_old_numeric_list._note: Plausible wrong implementation: the numeric test is the old substring list (#integer / #decimal / #double / #float) instead of BuiltInFunctions.isNumeric — the derived integer types (xsd:int, xsd:long, xsd:nonNegativeInteger, xsd:unsignedByte) become type errors. Specification: A19 and A21 (the derived types the substring list does not know — as a constant and from VALUES) turn red too.

M5_whole_string_numeric._note: Plausible wrong implementation 'reject only text that is not WHOLLY a number': a string goes through Number() — "7abc" errors, "7" still counts as 7. A2 stays green; every other text axis goes red. Specification: A16 (BIND("7" AS ?k) is wholly a number for Number()) turns red too.

M7_duration_branch_lenient._note: Strictness only in the standard numeric branch: the dayTimeDuration * number branch parses its other operand leniently again. Specification: A18 (a store literal and a date times a duration) turns red too.
M7_duration_branch_lenient.from:
const rightNum = this.toNumericValue(right);
      return BuiltInFunctions.durationMultiply(left, rightNum);
M7_duration_branch_lenient.to:
const rightNum = parseFloat(String((right as { value?: unknown })?.value ?? right));
      return BuiltInFunctions.durationMultiply(left, rightNum);

M8_left_operand_untyped._note: Independent review of the plan, HIGH: only the RIGHT operand keeps its numeric type — the left one is evaluated as before, so a numeric literal carried as text on the left (`1.5e0 + ?o`, an outer variable left of the operator in EXISTS / a bind join) is rejected. Every right-side axis stays green. Specification: A19 (its left-operand half) turns red too.

M9_right_operand_untyped._note: Mirror of M8: only the LEFT operand keeps its numeric type. Specification: A19 (its right-operand half) turns red too.

M10_nan_check_dropped._note: Independent review of the plan, MEDIUM: the `!isNaN` check of a numeric literal is dropped — `"abc"^^xsd:double + 1` becomes NaN instead of a type error (worse than 17.18.3, where it errors), COALESCE no longer moves on.

M11_operand_parsed_directly._note: Independent review of the plan, MEDIUM: the operand helper returns `parseFloat` of the lexical form instead of the typed literal — readable constants still count, an unreadable one becomes NaN. Shares its anchor with M3 — the driver applies every mutant to a clean copy.

M12_helper_keeps_any_type._note: Independent review of the spec, MEDIUM: the plan declared this mutant a zero (the isNumeric test 'defensive'). It is not: rebuilt as a typed literal, a constant of another datatype reaches the date / duration branches, where isDateTimeValue reads a Literal by its datatype IRI (`#date` anywhere) — "2026-11-10"^^<urn:x:dt#date> - "2026-11-01"^^<urn:x:dt#date> = P9D instead of an error. A20 locks it.
M12_helper_keeps_any_type.from:
const typed = new Literal(node.value, new IRI(node.datatype));
      if (BuiltInFunctions.isNumeric(typed)) {
M12_helper_keeps_any_type.to:
const typed = new Literal(node.value, new IRI(node.datatype));
      if (BuiltInFunctions.isNumeric(typed) || typed.datatype !== undefined) {

M13_strict_at_entry._note: Specification, matrix vs axes (integration-test-revert-verify §A159): no mutant held C3. Plausible wrong implementation 'reject a non-numeric operand at the ENTRY of evaluateArithmetic': both operands go through toNumericValue before the date / time / duration branches, so date - date, duration * number and number * duration become type errors. Strict, and wrong for every typed date and duration operand. C3 turns red by design; A11 too, because `1.5e0 * "PT1H"^^xsd:dayTimeDuration` (a number LEFT of a duration) goes through the number * duration branch, which the entry check now rejects.
M13_strict_at_entry.from:
const left = this.evaluateArithmeticOperand(expr.left, solution);
    const right = this.evaluateArithmeticOperand(expr.right, solution);

M14_only_js_numbers._note: Specification, matrix vs axes (§A159): no mutant held C2. Plausible wrong implementation 'an operand is numeric only if it is a JS number': a numeric Literal — a store xsd:integer / xsd:decimal value, a COUNT / SUM result, a typed constant rebuilt by evaluateArithmeticOperand — is rejected. The datatype test is replaced by one that never matches, so the shape of the expression (and its type narrowing) is kept. Wide by construction: every axis whose numeric operand arrives as a Literal goes red — C2 (store ?n / ?d, COUNT), C3 (duration * store ?n), A6 (COALESCE(?t + 1, ?n + 1) falls through to unbound), A8 / A11 (typed constants rebuilt as Literals), A9 / A12 (substituted store numbers), A14 (readable VALUES double), A15 (its control COUNT(?n + 0) = 2 drops to 0) and every path of A10. Specification: A19 and A21 turn red too (every typed numeric operand is a Literal).

M15_unbound_as_zero._note: Specification, matrix vs axes (§A159): no mutant held C4. Plausible wrong implementation 'an unbound operand counts as 0' (the COALESCE-like leniency): ?zzz + 1 = 1 instead of an error.

M16_var_numeric_string._note: Independent review of the spec, HIGH (CV): a plausible attempt to also fix c42f1a54 / N1 — a VARIABLE whose value is a string that is wholly a number counts as that number. Passes the 22 axes of the plan and the stand; brings the defect back for a text constant bound by BIND or projected by a subquery: BIND("7" AS ?k) ?k + 1 = 8.

M17_typed_whole_numeric._note: Independent review of the spec, HIGH (CS): a Literal of ANY datatype whose lexical form is wholly a number counts as that number. The plan's A4 constants reach arithmetic as JS strings, so no axis judged a Literal INSTANCE of a non-numeric datatype; VALUES {"7"^^xsd:string} ?v + 1 = 8, VALUES {"2026"^^xsd:gYear} ?v + 1 = 2027, GROUP_CONCAT(?o) + 1 = 8.

M18_duration_literal_lenient._note: Independent review of the spec, HIGH (CD): the three duration branches (duration * number, number * duration, duration / number) read a Literal operand with parseFloat. The plan's A7 used only a JS string "2"; a store literal "7", an xsd:dateTime and an xsd:date pass: "PT1H"^^xsd:dayTimeDuration * ?t = PT7H, * "2026-11-10"^^xsd:date = P84DT10H.

M19_short_type_list_constant._note: Independent review of the spec, MEDIUM (CT), constant half: the operand helper keeps the type only of the datatypes the plan's axes name plus the four primitives, instead of BuiltInFunctions.isNumeric; a constant of xsd:short, xsd:byte, xsd:positiveInteger, xsd:negativeInteger, xsd:nonPositiveInteger, xsd:unsignedLong / Int / Short becomes a type error.

M20_short_type_list_values._note: Independent review of the spec, MEDIUM (CT), value half: toNumericValue accepts only the short list of datatypes; a VALUES-bound literal of the other eight numeric datatypes becomes a type error. Shares its anchor with M14 / M17 — the driver applies every mutant to a clean copy. A19 turns red too: a constant of a short-list-missing type is rebuilt as a typed literal by the helper and then rejected here.
